title: Life Life Life
intro: Life Life Life gives its three performers different ways to answer what a life is worth. Yoyi makes having little into resistance to threats and empty promises. User116 turns toward staying alive and enjoying ordinary, unflattering appetites. Jackzebra enjoys the ease of making music with friends, then theatrically declares the entire contact list—and himself—dead. The same social feed holds pleasure and erasure. The final claim about fate is deliberately sweeping, but it lands after a record of people choosing, joking and making things together.
reading: Three distinct responses to life's value; shared platform and repeated word for life/fate connect them without erasing differences.

revisions.t42-phrase-worthless-life: Yoyi's opening deprives an imagined creditor or threatener of leverage: there is no money to take, only a life he has already called worthless. Later he says that same life is enviably good. The reversal shows self-devaluation functioning as a defence rather than a settled judgement of value. He can mock the price placed on him while still enjoying what cannot be cloned about his style.
revisions.editorial-42-sleep-routine: User116 turns from rebuking somebody into a series of small first-person recovery claims and self-instructions. The admission that it still hurts prevents the smiles and present-focused advice from proving an effortless transformation. This is one character's account of trying to live, including a personal statement about medication, rather than a universal formula. Its force comes from lowering the threshold of success to continued life and manageable pleasures.
revisions.t42-phrase-worldly: The verse refuses to make survival depend on becoming morally elevated. Good food, attraction, money and a pleasing social feed can matter to an ordinary person. The apparent contradiction between dismissing money and admitting greed is part of that human scale: he does not need one pure principle to explain every appetite. This gives the next verse's universal death announcement something recognisably enjoyable to wipe away.
revisions.t42-phrase-half-hour: Making songs quickly, when the mood arrives, presents creativity as accessible play with collaborators. The self-mocking howling and phonetic roll call keep the boast social and comic. This matters before the mass-erasure joke: the voice announcing that everybody is dead has just described something people make together. The collaboration remains evidence of activity and connection inside the lyric's exaggerated dismissal of the whole world.
revisions.t42-phrase-wechat-dead: User116 has filled the contact list with desirable people; Jackzebra uses the same platform to announce that all its people are dead. The exact count starts like a plausible inventory, then the sequence includes the announcer and every available pronoun. It is a totalising joke that leaves nobody outside to certify it. The shared feed makes opposite fantasies possible: having everybody available and having nobody left to demand anything.
